title: Resolution No. 245 (2023) – Regarding Procedures for Licensing Communication Stations and Towers Within Cooperative Societies
text:
Resolution No. (245/2023)
Issued on: April 5, 2023
Regarding Procedures for licensing
Communication Stations and Towers
within the Cooperative Societies
1 | Page

The Board of Directors,
- After reviewing Law No. (37) of 2014, regarding the establishment of the Communications
and Information Technology Regulatory Authority and its amendments,
- Decree No. (144) of 2022, on forming CITRA’s Board of Directors,
- Cabinet Resolution No. (993) of 2015, issued on 13/7/2015 on issuing the executive
regulations of Law No. (37) of 2014 for the establishment of the Communications and
Information Technology Regulatory Authority and its amendments,
- CITRA Board of Directors’ Decision No. (1/2020) issued on 8/1/2020, on issuing the
regulation for specifications and requirements for building and operating public radio
stations,
- CITRA Chairman’s Decision No. (68/2022) issued on 19/4/2022,
- Board of Directors’ meeting Decision No. (2/2023), and
- Based on the interest of Work
DECIDED
Article (1)
The procedures for licensing communication stations and towers within the
cooperative societies and their affiliated sites shall be subject to all provisions
contained in this decision.
Article (2)
The licensing procedures are as follows:
The licensee submits an application to the Communications and Information
Technology Regulatory Authority, provided that the application includes the
following:
a. The site details.
b. The technical details of the radio station.
c. The contract data regarding the communications tower’s construction site.
Article (3)
The application is studied by CITRA, and if the application is approved, CITRA gives
the licensee an initial approval, until the issuance of the required permits and
approvals and the completion of the procedures, which are as follows:
a. The building permit shall be approved by the Kuwait Municipality.
b. Electricity must be connected to the site by the Ministry of Electricity and
Water.
2 | Page

c. The optical fiber connection by the Ministry of Communications.
d. Certification of compliance with non-ionizing emission levels from the Ministry
of Health.
e. A no-objection certificate from the General Fire Force.
f. A no-objection certificate from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, if the
site is located within the airport area.
Article (4)
The licensee shall submit a final license application to the Authority including all
required licenses, approvals, and certificates, and a declaration of the radio station's
conformity with the data on which the initial approval was granted.
Article (5)
CITRA shall conduct a survey and conformity check, and the final license shall be
issued after the collection of fees by the Authority.
Article (6)
The licensees must notify the Authority of any change in the status of the radio
station, such as hosting another operator, and when renewing or terminating the
contract within a period not exceeding (10) working days.
Article (7)
All companies that own existing mobile communication towers within the scope of
cooperative societies and their affiliated sites must reconcile their conditions in light
of the provisions of this resolution within a period not exceeding (6) months from the
date on which this resolution enters into force.
Article (8)
The competent authorities shall implement this resolution, each within its capacity,
and publish it in the Official Gazette.
Omar Saud Al-Omar
Chairman
Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority
3 | Page

text:
Resolution No.: (58/2023)

Amending Resolution No. (67) of 2022
Concerning the Tariff for Transit Circuits and Data Hub
The Board of Directors,

The Board of Directors,
- After reviewing Law No. (37) of 2014, regarding the establishment of the Communications
and Information Technology Regulatory Authority and its amendments,
- Decree No. (144) of 2022, concerning forming the Board of Directors of the
Communications and Information Technology Regulatory Authority,
- Cabinet Resolution No. (993) of 2015, issued on 13/7/2015, on issuing the executive
regulations of Law No. (37) of 2014,
- The relevant Minister of Communications’ Decision No. (349/2014) regarding the tariff of
transit circuits,
- Chairman’s Decision No. (67) of 2022 issued on 24/4/2022 regarding the tariffs for the
transit circuits and data hub,
- CITRA Board of Directors’ decision taken at Meeting No. (1/2023), dated 31/1/2023
concerning the data hub tariff, and
- Based on the interest of Work;
DECIDED
Article (1)
The Data Hub’s tariff stipulated in Articles 2 and 3 of the Chairman’s Decision No.
(67) of 2022 shall be abolished.
Article (2)

(67) of 2022 shall continue to be effective.

The concerned authorities, each within its capacity, shall implement this decision,
while any provision contrary to it shall be rescinded. It shall be effective from the date
of its publication in the Official Gazette.
Omar Saud Al-Omar
Chairman

title: International Roaming Services Regulations
text:
International Roaming Services Regulations
This regulation was issued by the Communications & Information
Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA)
In the State of Kuwait
Version No.: 1.0
Regulation No. ____ of 2021

Article (1)
Definitions
In application of the provisions of this regulation, the words and phrases contained
therein shall have the same meanings as those set forth in Law No. 37 of 2014 and
its amendment (Law No. 98 of 2015) as well as its regulations. In addition, the
following words and phrases shall have the meanings set forth against each of
them, unless the context requires otherwise:
Law: Law No. 37 of 2014 and its amendment (Law No. 98 of 2015)
International Roaming Service: enabling the roaming subscriber, through his/her
mobile device, to send or receive an international roaming call or a roaming SMS,
or use the data roaming service while being outside Kuwait, in coordination
between the mobile telecommunication services provider and the network operator
in the host country.
Data Roaming Service: enabling the roaming subscriber to use exchange packets
of telecommunication data through the mobile device connected to the
telecommunications network in the host country, including sending and receipt of
multimedia messages, and does not include sending and receipt of calls or SMSs.
International roaming call: A mobile voice call made by the roaming subscriber
originating from the host country’s network and ending at a public
telecommunications network, whether inside or outside Kuwait, or a voice call,
received by the roaming subscriber, originating from a public telecommunications
network, whether inside or outside Kuwait, and ending at the host country’s
network.
Roaming SMS: A short text message sent by the roaming subscriber originating
from the host country’s network and ending at a public telecommunications
network, whether inside or outside Kuwait, or received by the roaming subscriber

and originating from a public telecommunications network, whether inside or
outside Kuwait, and ending at the host country’s network.
SMS Alert Messages: The short text message that mobile telecommunication
service providers are obligated to send to the roaming subscriber under these
regulations.
Host country’s network: A public terrestrial mobile telecommunications network
located outside Kuwait that allows the roaming subscriber to make and receive an
international roaming call, send and receive a roaming SMS or use data roaming
service in coordination with the mobile telecommunication service provider.
Subscriber: Any person who is a party of a contract with a public
telecommunications operator to provide telecommunications services.
Roaming subscriber: A subscriber that exists outside the State of Kuwait and for
whom the international roaming service has been activated.
Mobile Telecommunications Service Provider: The licensee who has obtained a
license to provide mobile telecommunications services by the Authority, and
provides the roaming subscriber with mobile telecommunications services upon the
activation of the service.

Article (2)
Scope of application of the Regulations’ provisions
The provisions of this regulation shall be applied to mobile telecommunication
service providers regarding the provision of international roaming services.
Article (3)
Controls for providing International Roaming Service
The mobile telecommunications service provider, when providing the international
roaming service, shall consider the following:
1. The mobile telecommunications service provider shall enable the subscriber
to use the international roaming service only after requesting such service by
the subscriber through the available communication channels (call center,
website, application, branches, etc.).
2. The mobile telecommunication service provider shall enable the subscriber
to use the data roaming service only after requesting such service separately
from the request of the international roaming calls service and other
telecommunication services.
3. The data roaming service shall be provided in the form of bundles to be clear
and limited in terms of value and quantity, and it shall not be provided by
paying for the service prices as per the consumption of capacities (outside
bundles).
4. Ensuring that the roaming subscriber is sufficiently informed, before and
after activating the service, about the tariff imposed on the international
roaming service.
5. The tariff of the international roaming service submitted to the subscriber
shall be in Kuwaiti dinars.
6. Enabling the roaming subscriber, through an appropriate means, to monitor
the use of the data roaming service and control the expenses resulting
therefrom, free of charge.
7. Providing all subscribers with data about suspending or activating the
international roaming service.

Article (4)
SMS Alert Message
The mobile telecommunications service provider shall provide the roaming
subscriber, if it enters any foreign country or upon its request, with an automatic
SMS alert message at the earliest and free of charge, provided that this message
shall include, via a free access online link or any other free means, the following
information in both Arabic and English languages:
1- The maximum tariff for making an international roaming call (in Kuwaiti
dinars).
2- The maximum tariff for receiving an international roaming call (in Kuwaiti
dinars).
3- The maximum tariff for sending a roaming SMS and the extent to which any
tariff is applied for receiving it (in Kuwaiti dinars).
4- Tariff and data of the activated data roaming service bundle (in Kuwaiti
dinars).
5- Details of the mobile telecommunications service provider’s website, how to
obtain all information related to the international roaming service tariff and
the list of countries and networks approved in each country by the means
provided by the service provider (the website, its specific application, live
chat and other means of communication).
6- How to access emergency services, with the ability to call the emergency
services numbers in the host country, free of charge.
7- Details and method of contacting the customer service center of the mobile
telecommunications service provider through the free communication
channels provided by the service provider (Livechat, WhatsApp and other
means of communication).
8- Choosing a specific service provider during the international roaming, and
reminding it to set up its device settings to choose the service provider.
9- Information about the available bundles that help to reduce the bill cost
during the international roaming, as well as how to subscribe thereon.

Article (5)
Tariff Updates
The mobile telecommunication service provider shall, as soon as possible, provide
the roaming subscriber, by an automatic SMS alert message containing free access
online link or any other free means, with any updates that may occur to the
applicable international roaming services’ tariff.
Article (6)
The financial credit limit for the international roaming services for the post-
payment category
A. The mobile communications service provider shall apply a monthly financial
limit of fifty dinars as a tariff due on the international roaming service for
the roaming subscriber contracting by the post-paid services system, unless
another financial limit is agreed upon.
B. The mobile communications service provider, if the roaming subscriber
exceeds the financial credit limit, shall notify it, via an automatic SMS alert
message sent to its transferred device, with the procedures to be followed to
continue benefiting from the international roaming service and the costs
resulted in each additional call unit. In the event that the roaming subscriber
does not respond to this notice, the mobile telecommunications service
provider shall immediately suspend providing the international roaming
service. However, in the event that the telecommunications service provider
does not commit to interrupting the service, the subscriber shall not be
charged with any additional amounts that exceed the monthly financial limit
specified in item (6/A).
C. The service provider shall notify the customer, through SMS that contains a
free access online link or any other free means, with the pricing and usage
details according to the service provider’s latest update.
D. The roaming subscriber may request the amendment or cancellation of the
financial credit limit through the means provided by the telecommunications

service provider, and the mobile telecommunications service provider’s
approval of the subscriber’s request is required (and the mobile
telecommunications service provider shall decide on the request within one
working day from receiving it free of charge, and the approval shall be
communicated to the subscriber by SMS). While amending or canceling the
financial credit limit shall not entail amending any of the other terms of
service.
E. Such agreement shall be substantiated by any means of proof, along with
showing the new credit limits for the subscriber to be referred to in the event
of any dispute between the subscriber and the mobile telecommunication
service provider.
Article (7)
Notices of the percentage of the financial credit limit usage and the remaining
balance
A. The mobile telecommunication service provider shall send a notification, by
an automatic SMS alert message, to the roaming subscriber who contracted
under the post-payment services system through its mobile device when the
use of the international roaming service reaches the following percentages,
calculated from the monthly financial credit limit (in Kuwaiti dinars), along
with showing the percentage of units used:
1. Fifty percent (50%).
2. Seventy-five percent (75%).
3. One hundred percent (100%).
B. The mobile telecommunication service provider shall notify the roaming
subscribers, who contracted under the pre-paid services system, of the
balance remaining in their accounts as a result of using the international
roaming service via an automatic SMS alert message after each use of the
international roaming service. While the subscriber shall not be charged any
additional amounts when the pre-paid balance runs out.

Article (8)
Compliance
Without prejudice to the provisions of any other law, In the event that the service
provider violates the provisions of this regulations or one of the licensing terms,
the Authority shall have the right to take the measures and penalties stipulated in
the Authority’s law.

title: Accredited Registrar Policy
text:
Accredited Registrar Policy
Public Sector Governance Department
Information Technology Sector
V. 1.0
1

October 2021
Table of Contents :
Topic Page
1. Definitions 6
2. Policy Objectives 6
3. General Terms 6
4. General Requirements for obtaining Accredited 7
Registrar License
5. Special Requirements for Accredited Registrar License 8
6. Obligations of the Accredited Registrar 10
7. Obligations of the Accredited Registrars towards 12
Registrants
8. Obligations Relevant to Registrants’ Information 15
9. Enforcement of Code 15
10. Policy Review 15
Annex (A) – Fees 16
Annex (B) – Technical Tests 17
2

1. Definitions
All terms and expressions used herein have been defined in the
implementing regulation for Country Code Top Level Domain
Registry (CCTLD) for the State of Kuwait as approved by the Board
of Directors of the Communication & Information Technology
Regulatory Authority (CITRA).
2. Policy Objectives
This policy aims to:
2.1 Set the requirements for obtaining the accredited registrar license
by CITRA.
2.2 Identify the duties, rights, and obligations of the accredited
registrars towards registrants and CITRA.
2.3 Identify the consequences against the accredited registrars in case
of violating this policy.
3. General Terms
3.1 The accredited registrar authorized to the Country Code Top Level
Domain Registry (CCTLD) for Kuwait shall give due attention to
the duties and services towards public users.
3.2 The domain names registration applications are processed by the
accredited registrars, not directly by CITRA.
3

3.3 Compliance with this policy is mandatory for all accredited
registrars. The enforcement of this policy shall be unified and
binding on all the accredited registrars without minimal
amendment or exception.
4. General Requirements for obtaining the Accredited Registrar
License
4.1 The applicant (accredited registrar) shall pay the fees referred to in
Annex (A) hereto.
4.2 The applicant (accredited registrar) shall submit all the required
documents and papers together with providing an
acknowledgment that such documents and papers are true, valid,
and full. Such documents must be updated upon the renewal of the
license.
4.3 The applicant (accredited registrar) must have its personal website
through which it can be linked to the registration system of the
Country Code Top Level Domain Registry (CCTLD) for the State
of Kuwait.
4.4 The applicant (accredited registrar) shall provide the electronic
payment service on its website for the domains selling service to
registrants.
4.5 The applicant (accredited registrar) shall sign a Non-Disclosure
Agreement with the Public Authority for Civil Information
(PACI).
4

4.6 The applicant shall pass the technical tests stipulated in Annex
(B). While CITRA has the right to re-conduct such tests on a
periodic or random basis as it deems appropriate to ensure the
quality of services.
4.7 The accredited registrar applications for a license shall be
submitted by registration and authentication on the electronic
services of CITRA.
5. Special Requirements for the Accredited Registrar License
5.1 Having passed the technical tests and paid the fees referred to in
the fees clause of Annex (A) hereto by the applicant, the applicant
shall be given a license valid for a maximum of one year only. The
commercial license of the applicant is required to be valid during
the licensing term.
5.2 The accredited registrar license may be renewed Sixty (60) days
prior to its expiration. The accredited registrar shall be reminded
and notified of its license's expiration as follows:
5.2.1 Initial notification is to be served Sixty (60) calendar days prior
to the license's expiration period.
5.2.2 A second notification is to be served Thirty (30) calendar days
prior to the license's expiration period.
5.2.3 Final notification is to be served upon expiration of the license.
5.3 The accredited registrar's systems are technically assessed during
the period it is applying for renewal of the license. Based on the
5

outcomes of such assessment, CITRA may decide whether to
renew or reject the license renewal application.
5.4 The accredited registrar shall notify CITRA under a certified
written letter if the accredited registrar is unwilling to renew the
accredited registrar's license at least Sixty (60) calendar days prior
to the cancellation activation request date.
5.5 CITRA may terminate the license if:
5.5.1 The accredited registrar fails to abide by the policies and
resolutions of CITRA, or for any other reason CITRA deems
appropriate;
5.5.2 The accredited registrar fails to comply with the financial
liabilities referred to herein;
5.5.3 The accredited registrar fails to pass the periodic or random
technical tests.
5.6 CITRA has the right to deal with and dispose of the registered
domains with the accredited registrar in case:
5.6.1 The accredited registrar's license is canceled;
5.6.2 The accredited registrar fails to renew the license;
5.6.3 The accredited registrar is removed from the registrars' list, or
the accredited registrar's works are suspended due to a penal
sanction approved by CITRA against the accredited registrar;
6

5.6.4 Due to administrative, regulatory, or technical reasons approved
by CITRA.
6. Obligations of the Accredited Registrar
6.1 The accredited registrar shall abide by all the provisions set forth
in the law, implementing regulations and resolutions relating to
the registration of domain names together with all the policies
issued by CITRA and any amendments made thereto.
6.2 The accredited registrar shall use the registration system of
CITRA properly to register the domain names together with all the
information and details the accredited registrar may have access to
through the system in its capacity as an accredited registrar.
6.3 The accredited registrar agrees to provide the registrants'
information registration and update services. The accredited
registrar shall declare that such information is true, complete, and
updated. The accredited registrar shall keep the registrants' domain
names on the registration system, and maintain the privacy of such
information.
6.4 The accredited registrar shall provide all the accreditation
requirements all during the contracting period.
6.5 The accredited registrar declares that its company's name, logo,
and website link will be published on CITRA website.
6.6 The accredited registrar undertakes to notify CITRA regarding any
claim, request. The complaint, legal action, or proceedings the
accredited registrar may receive, which is associated with the
domain name registration process, under a certified written
7

notification attached with all the documents proving such a receipt
within Three (3) working days having known the same.
6.7 The accredited registrar shall keep all the necessary technologies
and restrictions developed and updated to ensure that the
accredited registrar is properly and safely linked to the names
registration system of the Country Code Top Level Domain
Registry (CCTLD). The accredited registrar further ensures that all
the exchanged data between the accredited registrar system and
the registration system will be safe to avoid the disclosure and
hacks of such data to and by any third parties.
6.8 The accredited registrar shall be solely responsible in full for any
damages and claims that may arise due to breaching provisions of
this policy by the accredited registrar.
6.9 The accredited registrar declares that CITRA has the right, as it
considers proper, to terminate the processing of the applications
submitted by the accredited registrar for definite periods should
CITRA consider such action is necessary for keeping the
registration systems safe and stable.
6.10 The accredited registrar declares that CITRA has the right, at
any time, to technically perform inspections and auditing; and that
the domain name application may be rejected or suspended even
having been approved should the registrant is found to violate any
of the procedures, requirements, or policies issued by CITRA.
6.11 The accredited registrar undertakes that the information
provided by the registrant is true, complete, and updated.
8

7. Obligations of the Accredited Registrars towards Registrants
The accredited registrars shall:
7.1 Ensure the registration of the domain name only upon the request
of applicants, i.e. not to register the Internet domain for them
unless the usage of such names is for the company's businesses
and projects;
7.2 Ensure not to "store" the domain names, i.e. registration of
numerous domain names without receiving definite instructions
thereon from the applicant;
7.3 Ensure that the domain names are not registered or renewed (prior
to the receipt of an in advance application from the applicant or
the registrant) to avoid the registration of a domain name on behalf
of the applicant or the registrant, as the case may be, by a
competitor of the registrar, or to offer such domain names to the
potential applicants later;
7.4 Ensure non-renewal of an expired internet domain name without
an application that is submitted from the concerned registrant
only, unless expressly requested by the registrant for the automatic
renewal service.
7.5 Ensure the issuance of domain names licenses for one (1) year or
two (2) years only;
7.6 Ensure not to take any action that may lead to the prevention of
legal registration for any domain name.
9

7.7 Ensure that the registrants are notified that they must renew their
respective domain license by phone call, in writing, or emails to
the email addresses of the registrants;
7.8 Ensure that the registrants are notified of the special terms and
conditions for the related domain names licenses, and to provide
recent copies thereof whenever they are required to;
7.9 Ensure that the registrants are called for updating the information
registered in "domain names information service, WHO IS" if they
are not correct;
7.10 Ensure that neither renewal notification nor any other things
that may interpret the same sent to the registrant or any third party,
unless they are sent by the authorized registrar, or received by the
registrant or the person responsible for administrative
communications regarding the internet domain name;
7.11 Ensure that the accredited registrar is allowed to offer extra
services to the registrants, provided:
7.11.1 Not to insist on the registrant to replace the current register,
or set such replacement as a condition for any type of the
services to be offered.
7.11.2 To clearly refer to any type of services the accredited
registrar provides, and to the way such services are organized
whether provided as one package or separately to customers;
and set prices for such services separately;
10

7.11.3 Ensure the ability of the accredited registrar to provide the
services announced in any offer provided to the applicants or
potential registrants;
7.11.4 Ensure the explicit compliance towards applicants with the
domain names licenses as per the prices set by CITRA;
7.11.5 Ensure that prices for the registered domains are clearly
identified and separately from any additional services on the
invoices the accredited registrars provided to the registrants;
7.12 Ensure that the registrants are notified via their respective
websites or emails of any changes made to any policies that may
have any terms and conditions relating to the domain names
license;
7.13 Ensure a mechanism for handling the disputes and
complaints, and that they are available to complainants.
7.14 Ensure that the accredited registrar publishes a service
cancellation notification for the registrants if the services agreed
upon between both parties are canceled;
7.15 Ensure that customers' complaints are handled properly
within three (3) working days;
7.16 Ensure that the complaints are referred to CITRA, should the
accredited registrar fails to solve the same within the identified
period if such complaints are beyond the accredited registrar's
powers;
11

7.17 Ensure that the unwanted email messages (spam) would not
be sent to current or potential customers.
8. Obligations Relating to the Registrants' Information
The accredited registrars shall:
8.1 Ensure that the information provided to the registry applicants or
current registrants are accurate, complete, and correct;
8.2 Ensure the application of the domain names privacy policy of
CITRA and the applicable laws in the State of Kuwait;
8.3 Ensure compliance with any other laws or regulations relevant to
consumers in the State of Kuwait;
8.4 Ensure that the registrants' personal information kept with the
accredited registrars would not be sent to any third parties unless
CITRA requires the same.
9. Enforcement of Policy
The accredited registrars shall perform their duties and tasks in
accordance with this policy. The alleged violations of the policy
shall be addressed in accordance with Article (64) of the CITRA
Law.
10. Policy Review
The management may update this policy, at any time, where it
deems appropriate, including updating for explanation purposes.
12

11. Annex (A) – Fees
11.1 The technical tests fees of One Hundred and Fifty (KD 150)
Kuwaiti Dinars shall be paid upon submission of the application
for an accredited registrar license for the first time.
11.2 In the event that the applicant fails to pass the technical tests
within the period given, i.e. (60) sixty calendar days, the applicant
shall submit a new application and pay the required fees as
stipulated in Clause 11.1 hereinabove.
11.3 The accredited registrar shall pay the annual license fees of
Three Hundred (KD 300) Kuwaiti Dinars.
11.4 The license renewal application is not inclusive of the
technical tests fees.
13

12. Annex (B) – Technical Tests
12.1 The electronic login system shall be linked to the Public
Authority for Civil Information (PACI).
12.2 A website for domain management and registration shall be
created, on which the electronic payment service shall be
provided.
12.3 The following functions shall be performed using the
electronic linkage to the Country Code Top Level Domain
Registry (CCTLD) names for Kuwait:
12.3.1 Registration of a new domain name;
12.3.2 Removal of a domain name;
12.3.3 Transfer of a domain name to another accredited registrar;
12.3.4 Modify the domain name information including:
▪ Identity of the registrants
▪ Data of the domain names servers
14

title: Data Classification Policy
text:
Data Classification Policy
State of Kuwait
v 2.3
Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority
(CITRA)
1 | P age

Contents
Section Title Page
1 Terms and Definitions 3
2 Introduction 4
3 Data Classification Policy 4
2 | P age

1. Terms and Definitions:
The following terms and expressions, wherever mentioned in this document, shall have the meanings
assigned to them below. The definitions mentioned in the Communication and Information Technology
Regulatory Authority Law No. 37 of 2014 and as amended by Law No. 98 of 2015, its executive regulations,
and the ICT Terms and Definitions document.
Term Definition
It is information that is edited, modified, printed, or stored by means of
a computer, and this information is in the form of text, audio, pictures,
1.1 Data
or video files, or in the form of computer programs or digital
information in a language that the computer understands.
It includes information or a set of information, if collected, the identity
of the individual can be clearly and directly inferred. It also includes
any information that can be linked indirectly, like the location data for
1.2 Personal Data
a specific person, regardless of whether the identity of the individual is
clear or not from that information or from a combination of data from
that information.
It is the classification (or placement or arrangement) of data in
1.3 Data Classification appropriate security levels based on their sensitivity to determine the
best means to use, share, and protect them.
It may be an individual, government entity or one of its sectors, or a
private company or one of its sectors, where he owns certain data and
has the authority to process, amend, copy or store it (for example, the
human resources sector owns the data of the entity’s employees, the
1.4 Data Owner
information technology sector owns the infrastructure and applications
data, the finance department owns the salary data, the customer care
department owns the customers data, the procurement department owns
the purchase data, etc.).
The process of converting data from readable text to unreadable text,
1.5 Encryption where the encryption process is applied both during data storage and
when transferred over networks.
Any loss of data, misuse or disarrangement, access, and modification to
1.6 Data Breach
data by unauthorized persons, or disclosure to unauthorized persons.
3 | P age

2. Introduction
This policy outlines a methodology for data classification for the public and private sectors.
Which, when followed, leads to defining the acceptable level of security protection, ensuring
adherence to acceptable best practices, and determining the means for data handling,
transmission, and processing. Whereas the failure to follow any approach to classify data and
provide the necessary protection for each category would expose this data to various electronic
risks such as data leakage, wrong handling and sharing, or penetration.
2.1 Data Classification Objectives
2.1.1 Objective: classifying data into separate categories helps in better decisions making,
regarding data access and processing in line with the data classification levels mentioned
in this policy, which contributes in helping the government or private entities to take all
necessary measures to enhance the security and protection of their data and the personal
data they have of the individuals, in a consistent manner with the requirements and
institutions plans, laws and regulations applicable in the State of Kuwait.
2.1.2 Scope: the policy scope includes data that is processed, stored, modified, or transferred
by computer or smart devices, i.e., digital data (structured or unstructured), which
government and private entities create, collect, and maintain as part of their official
business functions and use or share for the purpose of providing public services.
Examples of structured data include individuals' data (such as personal or company data),
non-customer data (such as environmental data), and organizational data (such as human
resources, finance, and data related to assets and purchases). Unstructured data includes
text-based data (but not limited to word processor documents, presentation slides, photos,
video clips, and audio recordings), data of printed documents fall out of the scope of this
policy. As for the access of printing or copying digital data, they must be determined
based on the sensitivity of the content and according to the level of classification in which
they fall under.
3. Data Classification Policy
3.1 Policy Items
3.1.1 The data owner shall classify their data into at least four levels. Entities of a security or
military nature of the country are excluded from adherence to the classification levels
specified in this policy, and they have the option to classify their data as they see
appropriate. If the data owner has a different classification system, mapping must be
made to the classified data with the classification system mentioned in this policy.
3.1.2 The owner of the data is free to choose their data protection methods according to their
data classification, retention, collection, and processing schemes. The data owner must
4 | P age

also ensure that necessary protection is provided to their data storing scheme depending
on its classification, especially Tier 3 and Tier 4 data, to protect them from hacking.
3.1.3 The data owner is required to create and maintain a data catalog which should include
the metadata information and standards for its data in a unified format. This catalog
should also be updated periodically.
3.1.4 The data owner must encrypt all classified data that falls under Tier 3 and Tier 4 during
transmission from one government entity to another, or when transmitted between
different physical geographical locations of government entities; this applies to the
private sector as well.
3.1.5 The data owner must ensure that all data classified according to the third and fourth levels
are transferred or removed from data centers and servers before the disposition of the
equipment of data centers and servers hosting the data.
3.1.6 The data classification levels mentioned in this policy have been developed based on the
best regional and global practices, and the data owner is free to use other classification
levels if they are best suitable with the type of data they have, in accordance with
international best practices and standards such as NIST 800-53, NIST SP 800-60, ISO
27001, PCI DSS, and HIPAA to ensure the validity and quality of classification.
3.2 What to consider before starting the data classification process
3.2.1 Data gathering, auditing, and analyzing processes. Incomplete, vague, or ambiguous data
should be excluded or modified.
3.2.2 Considering the accuracy in sorting and placing data in the classification levels in
accordance with this policy, to determine and evaluate the risks on each level to ensure
the safety and protection of the data.
3.2.3 Forming a data classification team headed by the senior management or their
representatives, with the membership of the Director of Information Security, the
Director of the Information Technology Department, in addition to the directors of the
various departments that own or store the data of the entity, whether this data is personal
and belong to subscribers or data belonging to the entity itself. As this team is responsible
of classifying the data in the entity and labeling it according to its sensitivity level and in
line with what is stated in this policy.
3.2.4 In order to ensure the full implementation of data classification and to support the
unification of procedures between the various entities, the authorities must do what is
necessary towards developing a road map and an action plan that explains how to
implement the process of classifying data according to the four basic levels described in
this policy, provided that the data classifications is to be reviewed internally in an
appropriate periodic and fixed manner.
3.2.5 Determine and prioritize data sets, classify the data of high priority before other groups
of lower levels of priority, where priority level is according to the importance of the data,
5 | P age

its sensitivity and business value. This depends on the current data management maturity
level within the entity, the size of the entity’s operations, and the extent of data
importance to its functions.
3.2.6 Government and private sector entities shall be responsible for defining the roles and
responsibilities of the of its workforce, to implement the data classification policy within
its scope.
3.2.7 The roles and responsibilities for managing and classifying the data are determined
according to the discretion of each entity as it deems appropriate, as each entity differs
from the others in terms of infrastructure and procedures for managing the data. The
entity can decide to create new jobs to fulfill these roles or add responsibilities to the
current roles.
3.2.8 The sensitivity of the data should not be overemphasized.
3.3 Data Classification Tiers
Tier Description
Refers to unclassified data available to the public or data that is not
protected from public access under any law, regulation, or contract and
does not require any encryption, as it does not indicate the owner of the
data or has the impression of the government or private sector data. Some

"Public Data"

websites, daily newspapers, magazines, or other publications.
2. Self-service forms available to individuals and institutions.
3. General data and information publicly available on websites.

Refers to data owned by the public and private sectors or at a personal

1. First or last name
2. Job title, job duties and employer name

or home phone number
10. Address
Refers to data owned by the public and private sector or at a personal level.
It is data indicating the identity of the data owner, and related to the
content of the data owner, and may include part of the insensitive data,
and unauthorized disclosure leads to damage to the privacy of the data
owner. Examples include, but are not limited to:
The Third Tier: 1. Minutes of meeting and business plans
"Private Sensitive 2. Internal project reports
Data" 3. The files of the lawsuits and the preliminary and final provisions
issued therein, the decisions and orders of the courts and all related
files
4. Legal notes and opinions issued by legal offices
5. Medical records
6. Criminal fingerprint and DNA fingerprint
Refers to private data of a very sensitive nature, and the unauthorized
disclosure of this data may inflict great damage on the privacy of the
owner of the data. Or those data owned by the government or private sector
entities or at personal level of individuals or at the national level, and
therefore it should be published to a very specific segment of those who
The Fourth Tier: need access to it. This data must have high encryption requirements and
"Highly Sensitive requires the highest levels of protection and security. Some examples
Data" include, not limited to:
1. Encryption keys
2. Political documents, international negotiations, or international
relations data
3. Sensitive information of military nature or related to the state
security

3.4 Roles and Responsibilities
3.4.1 Roles and responsibilities of public and private sector entities who own their data
or individuals' data
All public and private sector entities must take the following into consideration when
classifying their data and the personal data of individuals they have.
Levels Description
1. Circulate this policy to the entity’s employees in its various sectors and
ensure that they understand its content and process the entity’s data in line
with this policy.
2. The entity or company must form a data classification team headed by the
senior management or their representatives, with the membership of each
of the director of information security department, the director of the
information technology department, in addition to the directors of the
various departments who own data, whether the data is personal and
pertains to subscribers or it is the entity or company data. As this team
classifies the data in the entity and label it according to its sensitivity level
in line with what is stated in this policy.

3. Directing the entity’s employees to immediately report any breach in the

4. Record breaches and take corrective actions.
5. Approving the classification provided by the data owner in the entity.
6. Monitor and confirm the entities’ compliance with what is stated in this
policy and the Data Classification and Handling Procedure Guide if issued
by the Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority
(CITRA).
7. Assign a focal point employee to communicate and provide the Central
Agency for Information Technology (CAIT) with quarterly reports on the
extent of implementation of this policy, as CAIT is the supervisor of the
implementation of the regulations and policies issued by CITRA.

technology department to provide a safe environment for hosting the data.
3. Make periodic reviews and evaluations of the classified data and amend it
if necessary.

1. Supporting the entity to implement the policy by providing technologies
Information that enable data owners at the entity to classify their data.
Technology 2. Provide the appropriate infrastructure and security standards to enable
Department classification and protection of data according to the requirements of
classification tiers mentioned in article 3.3 of this policy.
3.4.2 Roles and responsibilities of the Communication and Information Technology
Regulatory Authority (CITRA)
3.4.2.1 Issue policies and guidelines related to information and communication technology.
3.4.2.2 Monitor the public and private sectors entities in implementing the policies and
guidelines issued by the authority to ensure compliance.
3.4.2.3 Request periodic reports from the Central Agency for Information and Technology
(CAIT) to analyze and measure the compliance and implementation of government
entities with this policy. Reports to contain the following:
- A catalog of all the data available and hosted at the entity, which must include
metadata in a unified format.
- The documents that show the approved classification tiers followed by the entity with
explanation of the bases and criteria used to set the classification tiers.
- The documents that clarify of the methods used for data protection and encryption in
accordance with the classification system used when hosting, storing, and processing
data.
- The documents that show the locations of stored data according to classification tiers.
- The roadmap for data classification process, with action plans and operations of the
entity to ensure the accuracy and quality of the data classification.
- A periodical progress report on the extent of the achievement in accordance with
action plans and in line with this policy.
3.4.2.4 Coordinate with the Central Agency for Information and Technology (CAIT) to develop
an implementation plan within a period not exceeding three months from the execution
date of the policy, to enable the implementation of the policy with the government
entities. Provided that the conditions of government entities are to be reconciled in
accordance with this policy within a period not exceeding two years.
3.4.2.5 Hold workshops and awareness sessions to increase the awareness level and help entities
implement the policies and guidelines issued by the Communication and Information
Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA).

text:

2

Introduction
Having the objective to manage radio frequencies effectively and to
safeguard their efficient utilization, since radio frequencies are
limited natural resources and must be used rationally, efficiently
and economically, in conformity with the provisions of Radio
Regulations. The Communication and Information Technology
Regulatory Authority in accordance with the provision of article (21)
of the Constitution, which states that Natural resources and all
revenues therefrom are the property of the State. It shall ensure
their preservation and proper exploitation due regard being given
to the requirements of State security and the national economy.
The pursuant to Decree no. 37/2014, and taking into account the
obligations arising from the membership of The State of Kuwait in
the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), issues the Plan of
Frequency Bands Allocations (National Table of Frequency
Allocations).
The Radio Frequency Department is issuing the Plan following its
approval by the Communication and Information Technology
Regulatory Authority and in accordance with the obligations of the
State of Kuwait arising from international treaties and from the
membership of the State of Kuwait in international organizations.
This National Table of Frequency Allocations will be modified from
time to time dependent on the decisions and recommendations
made by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) member
states as well as the decisions and recommendations made by the
national authorities.
3

Disclaimer
The information in this document is made available by the
Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority
on the understanding that it is for information purposes only. It is
not intended to form the basis of any investment decision and
should not be considered as a recommendation by the others to
participate in any tender for the allocation of radio spectrum.
Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority
makes no representation or warranty nor accepts any responsibility
as to the accuracy or completeness of the information contained in
this document and any liability in respect of any such information or
any inaccuracy in, or omission from, this document is hereby
expressly disclaimed.
Recipients of this document in any format should obtain their own
professional, financial, legal or other advice to make an
independent assessment of the potential value of any allocation of
radio spectrum by whatever means applicable. The policy of the
Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority
is to correct and update the document at regular intervals.
Any reproduction of all or part of the document for any commercial
purpose is forbidden.
4

Terms and Definitions
For the purposes of the Plan, the following terms shall have the
meanings defined below.
These terms and definitions do not, however, necessarily apply for
other purposes.
Definitions identical to those contained in the Annex to the
Constitution or the Annex to the Convention of the International
Telecommunication Union (Geneva, 1992) are marked “(CS)” or
“(CV)” respectively.
A. General terms:
1- Administration: Any governmental department or service responsible
for discharging the obligations undertaken in the Constitution of the
International Telecommunication Union, in the Convention of the
International Telecommunication Union and in the Administrative
Regulations (CS 1002).
2- Telecommunication: Any transmission, emission or reception of
signs, signals, writings, images and sounds or intelligence of any
nature by wire, radio, optical or other electromagnetic systems (CS) .
3- Radio: A general term applied to the use of radio waves.
4- Radio waves or hertzian waves: Electromagnetic waves of
frequencies arbitrarily lower than 3 000 GHz, propagated in space
without artificial guide.
5- Radiocommunication: Telecommunication by means of radio waves
(CS) (CV).
6- Terrestrial radiocommunication: Any radiocommunication other
than space radiocommunication or radio astronomy.
7- Space radiocommunication: Any radiocommunication involving the
use of one or more space stations or the use of one or more reflecting
satellites or other objects in space.
8- Radiodetermination: The determination of the position, velocity
and/or other characteristics of an object, or the obtaining of
5

9- information relating to these parameters, by means of the propagation
properties of radio waves.
Radionavigation: Radiodetermination used for the purposes of navigation,
including obstruction warning.
10- Radiolocation: Radiodetermination used for purposes other than those
of radionavigation.
11- Radio direction-finding: Radiodetermination using the reception of
radio waves for determining the direction of a station or object.
12- Radio astronomy: Astronomy based on the reception of radio waves
of cosmic origin.
13- Co-ordinated Universal Time (UTC): Time scale, based on the
second (SI), as defined in ITU-R Recommendation ITU-R TF.460-5.
For most practical purposes associated with the RR, UTC is equivalent
to mean solar time at the prime meridian (0° longitude), formerly
expressed in GMT.
14- Industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) applications (of radio
frequency energy): Operation of equipment or appliances designed to
generate and use locally radio frequency energy for industrial,
scientific, medical, domestic or similar purposes, excluding
applications in the field of telecommunications.
B. Specific terms related to frequency management:
1- Allocation (of a frequency band): Entry in the table of frequency
allocations of a given frequency band for its use by one or more terrestrial
or space radiocommunication services or the radio astronomy service
under specified conditions. This term shall also be applied to the
frequency band concerned.
2- Allotment (of a radio frequency or radio frequency channel): Entry
of a designated frequency channel in an agreed plan, adopted by a
competent conference, for use by one or more administrations for a
terrestrial or space radiocommunication service in one or more identified
countries or geographical areas and under specified conditions.
3- Assignment (of a radio frequency or radio frequency channel):
Authorization given by an administration for a radio station to use a radio
frequency or radio frequency channel under specified conditions.
6

C. Radiocommunication services:
1- Radiocommunication service: A service as defined in this Section
involving the transmission, emission and/or reception of radio waves for
specific telecommunication purposes
2- Fixed service: A radiocommunication service between specified
fixed points.
3- Fixed-satellite service: A radiocommunication service between
earth stations at given positions, when one or more satellites are used.
4- Inter-satellite service: A radiocommunication service providing
links between artificial satellites.
5- Space operation service: A radiocommunication service
concerned exclusively with the operation of spacecraft, in particular
space tracking, space telemetry and space telecommand.
6- Mobile service: A radiocommunication service between mobile and
land stations, or between mobile stations.
7- Mobile-satellite service: A radiocommunication service: between
mobile earth stations and one or more space stations, or between space
stations used by this service; or between mobile earth stations by means
of one or more space stations.
8- Land mobile service: A mobile service between base stations and
land mobile stations, or between land mobile stations.
9- Maritime mobile service: A mobile service between coast stations
and ship stations, or between ship stations, or between associated on-
board communication stations; survival craft stations and emergency
positionindicating radiobeacon stations may also participate in this
service.
10-Maritime mobile-satellite service: A mobile-satellite service in which
mobile earth stations are located on board ships; survival craft stations
and emergency position-indicating radiobeacon stations may also
participate in this service.
11-Aeronautical mobile service: A mobile service between aeronautical
stations and aircraft stations, or between aircraft stations, in which
survival craft stations may participate; emergency position-indicating
radiobeacon stations may also participate in this service on designated
distress and emergency frequencies.
7

12-Aeronautical mobile (R) service: An aeronautical mobile service
reserved for communications relating to safety and regularity of flight,
primarily along national or international civil air routes.
13-Aeronautical mobile (OR) service: An aeronautical mobile service
intended for communications, including those relating to flight
coordination, primarily outside national or international civil air routes.
14-Aeronautical mobile-satellite service: A mobile-satellite service in
which mobile earth stations are located on board aircraft; survival craft
stations and emergency position-indicating radiobeacon stations may
also participate in this service.
15-Aeronautical mobile-satellite (R) service: An aeronautical
mobilesatellite service reserved for communications relating to safety
and regularity of flights, primarily along national or international civil
air routes.
16-Aaeronautical mobile-satellite (OR) service: An aeronautical
mobilesatellite service intended for communications, including those
relating to flight coordination, primarily outside national and
international civil air routes.
17-Broadcasting service: A radiocommunication service in which the
transmissions are intended for direct reception by the general public.
This service may include sound transmissions, television transmissions
or other types of transmission (CS).
18-Broadcasting-satellite service: A radiocommunication service in
which signals transmitted or retransmitted by space stations are intended
for direct reception by the general public.
19-Radiodetermination service: A radiocommunication service for the
purpose of radiodetermination.
20-Radiodetermination-satellite service: A radiocommunication service
for the purpose of radiodetermination involving the use of one or more
space stations.
21-Radionavigation service: A radiodetermination service for the purpose
of radionavigation.
22-Radionavigation-satellite service: A radiodetermination-satellite
service used for the purpose of radionavigation.
8

23-Maritime radionavigation service: A radionavigation service intended
for the benefit and for the safe operation of ships.
24-Maritime radionavigation-satellite service: A radionavigation-
satellite service in which earth stations are located on board ships.
25-Aeronautical radionavigation service: A radionavigation service
intended for the benefit and for the safe operation of aircraft.
26-Aeronautical radionavigation-satellite service: A
radionavigationsatellite service in which earth stations are located on
board aircraft.
27-Radiolocation service: A radiodetermination service for radiolocation.
28-Radiolocation-satellite service: A radiodetermination-satellite service
used for radiolocation.
29-Meteorological aids service: A radiocommunication service used for
meteorological, including hydrological, observations and exploration.
30-Earth exploration-satellite service: A radiocommunication service
between earth stations and one or more space stations, which may
include links between space stations.
31-Meteorological-satellite service: An earth exploration-satellite service
for meteorological purposes.
32-Standard frequency and time signal service: A radiocommunication
service for scientific, technical and other purposes, providing the
transmission of specified frequencies, time signals, or both, of stated
high precision, intended for general reception.
33-Standard frequency and time signal-satellite service: A
radiocommunication service using space stations on earth satellites for
the same purposes as those of the standard frequency and time signal
service.
34-Space research service: A radiocommunication service in which
spacecraft or other objects in space are used for scientific or
technological research purposes.
9

35-Amateur service: A radiocommunication service for the purpose of
selftraining, intercommunication and technical investigations carried out
by amateurs, that is, by duly authorized persons interested in radio
technique solely with a personal aim and without pecuniary interest.
36-Amateur-satellite service: A radiocommunication service using space
stations on earth satellites for the same purposes as those of the amateur
service.
37-Radio astronomy service: A service involving the use of radio astronomy.
38-Safety service: Any radiocommunication service used permanently or
temporarily for the safeguarding of human life and property.
39-Special service: A radiocommunication service, not otherwise defined in
this Section, carried on exclusively for specific needs of general utility,
and not open to public correspondence.
10

Frequency Bands
The radio spectrum is subdivided into nine frequency bands - as specified in
the international agreement of the International Telecommunication Union -,
which is designated by progressive whole numbers in accordance with the
following table:
1 VLF 3 to 30 kHz
2 LF 30 to 300 kHz
3 MF 300 to 3 000 kHz
4 HF 3 to 30 MHz
5 VHF 30 to 300 MHz
6 UHF 300 to 3 000 MHz
7 SHF 3 to 30 GHz
8 EHF 30 to 300 GHz
9 THF 300 to 3 000 GHz
1- The unit of frequency is the hertz (Hz), frequencies shall be expressed:
– in kilohertz (kHz), up to and including 3 000 kHz;
– in megahertz (MHz), above 3 MHz, up to and including 3 000
MHz; – in gigahertz (GHz), above 3 GHz, up to and including
3 000 GHz.
2- In the application of the Radio Regulations, Kuwait administration uses the
following units according to and as been used by the Radiocommunication
Bureau(ITU) :
– kHz for frequencies up to 28 000 kHz inclusive
– MHz for frequencies above 28 000 kHz up to 10 500 MHz
inclusive – GHz for frequencies above 10 500 MHz.
11

Frequency Allocations
Introduction
The following definitions are reported from ITU-RR and are relevant in the
context of the Kuwait national frequency table;
allocation (of a frequency band): Entry in the Table of Frequency Allocations
of a given frequency band for the purpose of its use by one or more terrestrial
or space radiocommunication services or the radio astronomy service under
specified conditions. This term shall also be applied to the frequency band
concerned.
allotment (of a radio frequency or radio frequency channel): Entry of a
designated frequency channel in an agreed plan, adopted by a competent
conference, for use by one or more administrations for a terrestrial or space
radiocommunication service in one or more identified countries or
geographical areas and under specified conditions.
assignment (of a radio frequency or radio frequency channel): Authorization
given by an administration for a radio station to use a radio frequency or radio
frequency channel under specified conditions.
12

Regions and areas
For the allocation of frequencies, the world has been divided into three Regions
(Kuwait is in Region1) as shown on the following map and described in Nos. 1 to 6:
1- Region 1: Region 1 includes the area limited on the east by line A (lines A,
B and C are defined below) and on the west by line B, excluding any of the
territory of the Islamic Republic of Iran which lies between these limits. It also
includes the whole of the territory of Armenia, Azerbaijan, the Russian
Federation, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan,
Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Turkey and Ukraine and the area to the north of
Russian Federation which lies between lines A and C.
2- Region 2: Region 2 includes the area limited on the east by line B and on
the west by line C.
3- Region 3: Region 3 includes the area limited on the east by line C and on
the west by line A, except any of the territory of Armenia, Azerbaijan, the
Russian Federation, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan,
Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Turkey and Ukraine and the area to the north of
Russian Federation. It also includes that part of the territory of the Islamic
Republic of Iran lying outside of those limits.
13

The lines A, B and C are defined as follows:
4- Line A: Line A extends from the North Pole along meridian 40° East of
Greenwich to parallel 40° North; thence by great circle arc to the intersection of
meridian 60° East and the Tropic of Cancer; thence along the meridian 60° East
to the South Pole.
5- Line B: Line B extends from the North Pole along meridian 10° West of
Greenwich to its intersection with parallel 72° North; thence by great circle arc
to the intersection of meridian 50° West and parallel 40° North; thence by great
circle arc to the intersection of meridian 20° West and parallel 10° South; thence
along meridian 20° West to the South Pole.
6- Line C: Line C extends from the North Pole by great circle arc to the
intersection of parallel 65° 30′ North with the international boundary in Bering
Strait; thence by great circle arc to the intersection of meridian 165° East of
Greenwich and parallel 50° North; thence by great circle arc to the intersection
of meridian 170° West and parallel 10° North; thence along parallel 10° North
to its intersection with meridian 120° West; thence along meridian 120° West to
the South Pole
Categories of Services and Allocations:
A. Primary and secondary services
1- Where, in a box of the table, a band is indicated as allocated to more
than one service, either on a worldwide or Regional basis, such services
are listed in the following order:
a- If the names of services are printed in capital characters, it is called
a
primary service. (example: FIXED).
b- If the names of services are printed in small characters, it is called
a
secondary service. (example: Mobile).
2- Additional remarks shall be printed in normal characters (example:
MOBILE except aeronautical mobile).
14

3- Stations of a secondary service
a. shall not cause harmful interference to stations of primary
service,
b. cannot claim protection from harmful interference from stations of
primary service and,
c. can only claim protection from harmful interference of same or other
secondary service(s).
4- Where a band is indicated in a footnote of the table as allocated to a
service “on a secondary basis” in an area smaller than a Region, or in a
particular country, this is a secondary service.
5- Where a band is indicated in a footnote of the Table as allocated to a
service “on a primary basis”, in an area smaller than a Region, or in a
particular country, this is a primary service only in that area or country.
B. Additional allocations
1- Where a band is indicated in a footnote of the table as “also
allocated” to a service in an area smaller than a Region, or in a particular
country, this is an “additional” allocation, i.e. an added allocation in this
area or in this country to the service or services which are indicated in
the table (see No. 2).
2- If the footnote does not include any restriction on the service or
services concerned apart from the restriction to operate only in a
particular area or country,
stations of this service or these services shall have equality of right to
operate with stations of the other primary service or services indicated
in the table.
3- If restrictions are imposed on an additional allocation in addition to
the restriction to operate only in a particular area or country, this is
indicated in the footnote of the table.
15

C. Alternative allocations
1- Where a band is indicated in a footnote of the table as “allocated” to
one or more services in an area smaller than a Region, or in a particular
country, this is an “alternative” allocation, i.e. an allocation which
replaces, in this area or in this country, the allocation indicated in the
table (see No. 2).
2- If the footnote does not include any restriction on stations of the
service or services concerned, apart from the restriction to operate only
in a particular area or country, these stations of such a service or services
shall have an equality of right to operate with stations of the primary
service or services, indicated in the table, to which the band is allocated
in other areas or countries.
3- If restrictions are imposed on stations of a service to which an
alternative allocation is made, in addition to the restriction to operate only
in a particular country or area, this is indicated in the footnote.

text:
Data Classification Policy
State of Kuwait
v 2.3
Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority
(CITRA)

Contents
Section Title Page
1 Terms and Definitions 3
2 Introduction 4
3 Data Classification Policy 4

1. Terms and Definitions:
The following terms and expressions, wherever mentioned in this document, shall have the meanings
assigned to them below. The definitions mentioned in the Communication and Information Technology
Regulatory Authority Law No. 37 of 2014 and as amended by Law No. 98 of 2015, its executive regulations,
and the ICT Terms and Definitions document.
Term Definition
It is information that is edited, modified, printed, or stored by means of
a computer, and this information is in the form of text, audio, pictures,
1.1 Data
or video files, or in the form of computer programs or digital
information in a language that the computer understands.
It includes information or a set of information, if collected, the identity
of the individual can be clearly and directly inferred. It also includes
any information that can be linked indirectly, like the location data for
1.2 Personal Data
a specific person, regardless of whether the identity of the individual is
clear or not from that information or from a combination of data from
that information.
It is the classification (or placement or arrangement) of data in
1.3 Data Classification appropriate security levels based on their sensitivity to determine the
best means to use, share, and protect them.
It may be an individual, government entity or one of its sectors, or a
private company or one of its sectors, where he owns certain data and
has the authority to process, amend, copy or store it (for example, the
human resources sector owns the data of the entity’s employees, the
1.4 Data Owner
information technology sector owns the infrastructure and applications
data, the finance department owns the salary data, the customer care
department owns the customers data, the procurement department owns
the purchase data, etc.).
The process of converting data from readable text to unreadable text,
1.5 Encryption where the encryption process is applied both during data storage and
when transferred over networks.
Any loss of data, misuse or disarrangement, access, and modification to
1.6 Data Breach
data by unauthorized persons, or disclosure to unauthorized persons.
3 | P age

2. Introduction
This policy outlines a methodology for data classification for the public and private sectors.
Which, when followed, leads to defining the acceptable level of security protection, ensuring
adherence to acceptable best practices, and determining the means for data handling,
transmission, and processing. Whereas the failure to follow any approach to classify data and
provide the necessary protection for each category would expose this data to various electronic
risks such as data leakage, wrong handling and sharing, or penetration.
2.1 Data Classification Objectives
2.1.1 Objective: classifying data into separate categories helps in better decisions making,
regarding data access and processing in line with the data classification levels mentioned
in this policy, which contributes in helping the government or private entities to take all
necessary measures to enhance the security and protection of their data and the personal
data they have of the individuals, in a consistent manner with the requirements and
institutions plans, laws and regulations applicable in the State of Kuwait.
2.1.2 Scope: the policy scope includes data that is processed, stored, modified, or transferred
by computer or smart devices, i.e., digital data (structured or unstructured), which
government and private entities create, collect, and maintain as part of their official
business functions and use or share for the purpose of providing public services.
Examples of structured data include individuals' data (such as personal or company data),
non-customer data (such as environmental data), and organizational data (such as human
resources, finance, and data related to assets and purchases). Unstructured data includes
text-based data (but not limited to word processor documents, presentation slides, photos,
video clips, and audio recordings), data of printed documents fall out of the scope of this
policy. As for the access of printing or copying digital data, they must be determined
based on the sensitivity of the content and according to the level of classification in which
they fall under.
3. Data Classification Policy
3.1 Policy Items
3.1.1 The data owner shall classify their data into at least four levels. Entities of a security or
military nature of the country are excluded from adherence to the classification levels
specified in this policy, and they have the option to classify their data as they see
appropriate. If the data owner has a different classification system, mapping must be
made to the classified data with the classification system mentioned in this policy.
3.1.2 The owner of the data is free to choose their data protection methods according to their
data classification, retention, collection, and processing schemes. The data owner must
4 | P age

also ensure that necessary protection is provided to their data storing scheme depending
on its classification, especially Tier 3 and Tier 4 data, to protect them from hacking.
3.1.3 The data owner is required to create and maintain a data catalog which should include
the metadata information and standards for its data in a unified format. This catalog
should also be updated periodically.
3.1.4 The data owner must encrypt all classified data that falls under Tier 3 and Tier 4 during
transmission from one government entity to another, or when transmitted between
different physical geographical locations of government entities; this applies to the
private sector as well.
3.1.5 The data owner must ensure that all data classified according to the third and fourth levels
are transferred or removed from data centers and servers before the disposition of the
equipment of data centers and servers hosting the data.
3.1.6 The data classification levels mentioned in this policy have been developed based on the
best regional and global practices, and the data owner is free to use other classification
levels if they are best suitable with the type of data they have, in accordance with
international best practices and standards such as NIST 800-53, NIST SP 800-60, ISO
27001, PCI DSS, and HIPAA to ensure the validity and quality of classification.
3.2 What to consider before starting the data classification process
3.2.1 Data gathering, auditing, and analyzing processes. Incomplete, vague, or ambiguous data
should be excluded or modified.
3.2.2 Considering the accuracy in sorting and placing data in the classification levels in
accordance with this policy, to determine and evaluate the risks on each level to ensure
the safety and protection of the data.
3.2.3 Forming a data classification team headed by the senior management or their
representatives, with the membership of the Director of Information Security, the
Director of the Information Technology Department, in addition to the directors of the
various departments that own or store the data of the entity, whether this data is personal
and belong to subscribers or data belonging to the entity itself. As this team is responsible
of classifying the data in the entity and labeling it according to its sensitivity level and in
line with what is stated in this policy.
3.2.4 In order to ensure the full implementation of data classification and to support the
unification of procedures between the various entities, the authorities must do what is
necessary towards developing a road map and an action plan that explains how to
implement the process of classifying data according to the four basic levels described in
this policy, provided that the data classifications is to be reviewed internally in an
appropriate periodic and fixed manner.
3.2.5 Determine and prioritize data sets, classify the data of high priority before other groups
of lower levels of priority, where priority level is according to the importance of the data,
5 | P age

its sensitivity and business value. This depends on the current data management maturity
level within the entity, the size of the entity’s operations, and the extent of data
importance to its functions.
3.2.6 Government and private sector entities shall be responsible for defining the roles and
responsibilities of the of its workforce, to implement the data classification policy within
its scope.
3.2.7 The roles and responsibilities for managing and classifying the data are determined
according to the discretion of each entity as it deems appropriate, as each entity differs
from the others in terms of infrastructure and procedures for managing the data. The
entity can decide to create new jobs to fulfill these roles or add responsibilities to the
current roles.
3.2.8 The sensitivity of the data should not be overemphasized.
3.3 Data Classification Tiers
Tier Description
Refers to unclassified data available to the public or data that is not
protected from public access under any law, regulation, or contract and
does not require any encryption, as it does not indicate the owner of the
data or has the impression of the government or private sector data. Some
The First Tier:
examples include:
"Public Data"
1. Open data such as policies, regulations and laws published on
websites, daily newspapers, magazines, or other publications.
2. Self-service forms available to individuals and institutions.
3. General data and information publicly available on websites.
6 | P age

Refers to data owned by the public and private sectors or at a personal
level. It is data that indicates insensitive private data that indicates the
identity of the data owner, and unauthorized disclosure does not lead to
any damage to the privacy of the data owner. Examples include, but are
not limited to:
1. First or last name
2. Job title, job duties and employer name
The Second Tier:
3. E-mail address

Insensitive Data"

6. Age
7. Academic qualification
8. Social status
9. Contact data such as: work phone number, mobile phone number,
or home phone number
10. Address
Refers to data owned by the public and private sector or at a personal level.
It is data indicating the identity of the data owner, and related to the
content of the data owner, and may include part of the insensitive data,
and unauthorized disclosure leads to damage to the privacy of the data
owner. Examples include, but are not limited to:
The Third Tier: 1. Minutes of meeting and business plans
"Private Sensitive 2. Internal project reports
Data" 3. The files of the lawsuits and the preliminary and final provisions
issued therein, the decisions and orders of the courts and all related
files
4. Legal notes and opinions issued by legal offices
5. Medical records
6. Criminal fingerprint and DNA fingerprint
Refers to private data of a very sensitive nature, and the unauthorized
disclosure of this data may inflict great damage on the privacy of the
owner of the data. Or those data owned by the government or private sector
entities or at personal level of individuals or at the national level, and
therefore it should be published to a very specific segment of those who
The Fourth Tier: need access to it. This data must have high encryption requirements and
"Highly Sensitive requires the highest levels of protection and security. Some examples
Data" include, not limited to:
1. Encryption keys
2. Political documents, international negotiations, or international
relations data
3. Sensitive information of military nature or related to the state
security
7 | P age

3.4 Roles and Responsibilities
3.4.1 Roles and responsibilities of public and private sector entities who own their data
or individuals' data
All public and private sector entities must take the following into consideration when
classifying their data and the personal data of individuals they have.
Levels Description
1. Circulate this policy to the entity’s employees in its various sectors and
ensure that they understand its content and process the entity’s data in line
with this policy.
2. The entity or company must form a data classification team headed by the
senior management or their representatives, with the membership of each
of the director of information security department, the director of the
information technology department, in addition to the directors of the
various departments who own data, whether the data is personal and
pertains to subscribers or it is the entity or company data. As this team
classifies the data in the entity and label it according to its sensitivity level
in line with what is stated in this policy.

3. Directing the entity’s employees to immediately report any breach in the
Management
implementation of this policy.
4. Record breaches and take corrective actions.
5. Approving the classification provided by the data owner in the entity.
6. Monitor and confirm the entities’ compliance with what is stated in this
policy and the Data Classification and Handling Procedure Guide if issued
by the Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority
(CITRA).
7. Assign a focal point employee to communicate and provide the Central
Agency for Information Technology (CAIT) with quarterly reports on the
extent of implementation of this policy, as CAIT is the supervisor of the
implementation of the regulations and policies issued by CITRA.
